name: A minor pentatonic — box 1
position: Box 1 · frets 5–8, root on string 6 fret 5
description: The box every blues player starts with. Index finger on fret 5, ring or little finger on 7 and 8. Wraps around the E-shape Am barre.

name: A minor pentatonic — box 2
description: Starts where box 1's top notes end. Roots on string 4 fret 7 and string 2 fret 10.

name: A minor pentatonic — box 3
description: Root on string 5 fret 12. The G–B kink is the step from fret 9/12 on string 3 to 10/13 on string 2.

name: A minor pentatonic — box 4
description: Wraps around the A-shape Am barre at fret 12. Roots on string 5 fret 12 and string 3 fret 14.

name: A minor pentatonic — box 5
description: The box just below box 1. Its top edge (fret 5) is box 1's bottom edge, so the five boxes form a loop.

name: A minor pentatonic — whole neck
description: All five boxes joined up. Find the squares (A) first; every box is built around them.

name: C major pentatonic — whole neck
description: The same dots as A minor pentatonic. Only the squares move — C is home now, so box 2 of A minor is box 1 of C major.

name: G major pentatonic — root on string 6
description: E minor pentatonic box 2, re-rooted on G: the same dots, with G as home. Major pentatonic is the country-and-soul sound under major chords.

name: A blues scale — box 1
description: Minor pentatonic plus the ♭5 (E♭), the passing note between the 4 and the 5.
